title: Cooling more while dissipating less: anomalous tradeoffs from thermodynamic geometry
authors: Andrea Canzio, Vasco Cavina, Salvatore Raia, Vito Vetrano, Matteo Scandi, Paolo Abiuso
abstract: We show that, starting from the same state, optimal driving can sometimes reach a colder (or hotter) target in the same amount of time while dissipating less energy, or equivalently dissipate the same amount of energy in a shorter time. We study this counterintuitive phenomenon in the slow-driving regime of an open quantum system, where we name it Near-Equilibrium Anomalous Tradeoff (NEAT). We establish necessary conditions for its occurrence and show its underlying geometric origin. While NEAT is reminiscent of the well-known Mpemba effect, the two phenomena are distinct in general. We demonstrate NEAT in an exactly solvable qutrit model, as well as for d-dimensional birth-death dynamics with independently controlled energy levels. Finally, we show how NEAT can improve the performance of Carnot engines.
summary: This paper introduces the Near-Equilibrium Anomalous Tradeoff (NEAT), a counterintuitive effect in open quantum systems where cooling or heating can be achieved with unexpectedly low energy dissipation. Using geometric tools derived from the thermodynamic length, the authors establish necessary conditions for NEAT and demonstrate its practical application in enhancing the performance of quantum heat engines.
main_problem: The paper investigates the Near-Equilibrium Anomalous Tradeoff (NEAT), a counterintuitive phenomenon where optimal quantum driving can achieve target states with less energy dissipation or in less time than expected.
main_result: NEAT is characterized by a geometric condition related to the thermodynamic length, showing that the minimum dissipation cost is not always monotonic with the temperature difference.
method: The analysis uses geometric methods, relating minimum dissipation to the thermodynamic length metric derived from the slow-driving limit of the quantum master equation.
model_or_system: The study applies to open quantum systems undergoing thermalization, modeled by GKSL master equations. Specific examples include qutrit models and d-dimensional birth-death dynamics.

main_assumptions: The dynamics are assumed to be governed by a GKSL thermalizing Markovian master equation, and the analysis relies on the slow-driving/low-dissipation limit.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate cooling protocols, comparing different control paths, and show the geometric relationship between the Gibbs cooling curve and the optimal paths exhibiting the NEAT effect.
paper_structure: The paper first defines NEAT and establishes its necessary geometric conditions. It then demonstrates the effect in solvable models (qutrit, birth-death) and finally applies the concept to improve the performance of finite-time heat engines like the Carnot cycle.
why_interesting: This work provides a deep geometric understanding of non-equilibrium thermodynamics, showing how quantum control can violate expected monotonic relationships between work, time, and dissipation, which is crucial for designing efficient quantum thermal machines.
